question: Does the Vercel AI SDK Claude Code harness place bridge-control credentials in the environment inherited by the Claude Agent SDK runtime, and does possession of those credentials authorize a second bridge socket to replace the host connection and submit control frames?

sources.name: Vercel AI SDK Claude Code harness
sources.claim: The sandbox bridge process receives BRIDGE_CHANNEL_TOKEN and BRIDGE_WS_PORT in its environment.

sources.name: Vercel AI SDK Claude Code bridge
sources.claim: The bridge gives the Claude Agent SDK its inherited process environment, explicitly merging process.env when caller env overrides are configured.

sources.name: Vercel AI SDK shared harness bridge runtime
sources.claim: The bridge authenticates sockets by the token, replaces the active socket with each newly authorized connection, supports replay, and accepts approval/result/abort/stop/destroy control frames from the active authorized socket.

sources.name: Claude Platform Bash tool
sources.claim: Anthropic documents Bash as a persistent shell capability with access to environment variables and the working directory.

sources.name: Claude Agent SDK TypeScript release v0.3.149
sources.claim: Anthropic clarified that Options.env replaces the subprocess environment rather than merging with process.env; Vercel explicitly merges process.env before supplying custom env.

distinguishing_outcomes.observation: The source-derived child environment contains BRIDGE_CHANNEL_TOKEN and BRIDGE_WS_PORT.
distinguishing_outcomes.interpretation: The bridge credential and locator cross from bridge transport configuration into the model runtime environment in the modeled path.

distinguishing_outcomes.observation: An unauthorized replacement socket is rejected while an authorized replacement socket becomes active and can resolve a pending approval after replay.
distinguishing_outcomes.interpretation: Possession of the bridge credential confers the same bridge-control authority used by the host connection in the modeled shared runtime.

stop_condition: Stop once source, official runtime/tool contracts, one negative-control model, and a target-native test plan establish the narrow authority question without claiming an unexecuted exploit path.
